name: UK Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024
description: Statutory rules covering the UK DMCC Act 2024 mandatory pre-renewal disclosure schedules and 14-day cooling-off rights for UK consumers (prospective regime, anticipated commencement Spring 2027).

rules.title: Prospective Pre-Renewal Reminder Schedule (DMCC Spring 2027)

statute.title: Subscription Contracts — Pre-Renewal Reminders (Commencement Spring 2027)
statute.plainExplanation: The UK DMCC Act 2024 (Part 4, Chapter 2; anticipated commencement Spring 2027) mandates that traders send conspicuous pre-renewal reminder notices before consumer subscription renewal or trial rollover.

rules.explanation: The terms state or imply that the subscription will auto-renew without advance reminder notices. Note: under the prospective UK DMCC Act 2024 regime (Part 4, Chapter 2, anticipated commencement Spring 2027), traders will be required to provide advance reminder notices before renewal charges.
rules.recommendation: Verify that the trader commits to advance reminder notices before renewal. Under the upcoming UK DMCC regime, failure to provide statutory reminders will render subscription renewal terms unenforceable.

rules.title: Prospective 14-Day Cooling-Off Rights Obstruction (DMCC Spring 2027)

statute.code: UK DMCC Act 2024, Part 4, Chapter 2 (Cancellation Rights)
statute.title: 14-Day Subscription Cooling-Off Rights (Commencement Spring 2027)
statute.plainExplanation: UK consumers possess an unwaivable statutory right to cancel a subscription contract within a 14-day cooling-off window at inception and upon each 12-month renewal.

rules.explanation: The contract denies, restricts, or claims to waive 14-day cooling-off cancellation rights. Note: under the prospective UK DMCC Act 2024 regime (Part 4, Chapter 2, anticipated commencement Spring 2027), traders will be strictly prohibited from excluding statutory 14-day withdrawal windows.
rules.recommendation: Do not waive cooling-off cancellation rights. The upcoming DMCC Act regime will prohibit traders from excluding statutory 14-day withdrawal windows for consumer subscriptions.

rules.title: Unilateral Variation of Material Subscription Terms

statute.title: Unfair Contract Terms — Unilateral Variations
statute.plainExplanation: Terms granting traders unlimited unilateral discretion to alter subscription pricing, deliverables, or material specifications without consumer opt-out are presumptively unfair.

rules.explanation: The contract reserves unrestricted powers to alter prices or core subscription terms unilaterally without reasonable advance notice.
rules.recommendation: Under the UK Consumer Rights Act 2015, unfair price variation clauses are legally unenforceable against consumer subscribers.
